report:
Reviewed the complete syntax_identities claim, all four ordinary implementation associations, one ordinary test, and the explicit TODO test. Captured the linked Tree-sitter rationale, fixture/root setup, and parse span utilities. No source edits were made.

parse_str_to_cst creates temporary Tree-sitter parser/tree machinery and returns a Vec<LocalModItemSym>, not Tree-sitter identities. parse_item_list dispatches represented top-level syntax in source iteration order, retains pending attributes on their owning item, rejects tree nodes with errors, and converts unknown/unsupported top-level nodes and trailing unsupported attributes into explicit Error entries. parse/items.rs constructs per-item owned CST data with scope and absolute ParseSource provenance; macro invocation syntax stores path/input tokens without resolving its macro. Inline module children are parsed under ScopeSymbol::Module(new_module), while file-backed modules defer membership parsing. mods.rs unexpanded_items parses file-backed text with the module itself as scope. LocalStructSym demonstrates a stable name/scope identity with tracked CST/span detail and separately demanded sig/fields operations; its signature resolution and field checking are downstream calls, not parse actions. LocalModSym has the same identity/detail separation and a distinct membership query. Captured span utilities preserve supplied source provenance and item-relative syntax placement.

The current mods.rs edit only exposes symbol_local_item and adds a final-import-validation association; parsing, module ownership, identity fields and publication stay unchanged. All four associated files account for the stated parse architecture. This inspection does not imply every Rust syntax form is represented: unsupported syntax remains explicit recovery, and the current test coverage is intentionally partial.

The ordinary items_in_a_file_backed_module_use_that_module_as_their_scope fixture supplies lib.rs containing mod child and child.rs containing Holder. It finds the actual child module and struct via expanded membership and asserts Holder.scope equals that child module. Captured helpers register both real source files, parse the root and specify membership; the assertion therefore catches accidentally assigning file-module contents to the parent scope. It does not prove ordering, generated provenance, persistent identity stability, all recovery forms, or a parse-only execution firewall.

The modules_parse_syntax_identities TODO explicitly retains those missing source/generated fixture and query-trace cases: item order, ownership, CST/provenance, explicit malformed/unsupported recovery, and absence of resolution/signature/body/solver work in parse-only traces. Completing source/generated multi-item fixtures with direct CST/provenance assertions and a parse-only trace remains its prerequisite. This no-op is deferred evidence, not executable verification; no N/A entries apply.

Executed cargo test -p sage-test-harness --lib items_in_a_file_backed_module_use_that_module_as_their_scope: 1 passed, zero failures. Source inspection plus the concrete scope assertion and explicit remaining verification TODO account for the current claim without claiming full behavioral coverage. No edits requested.
